evals.name: music
evals.prompt: A "Now playing" screen for a music app called "Tempo". It must work and adapt across phone (411x923), foldable (933x704), tablet (1280x800), and desktop (1920x1080) windows; light and dark should both work. Show the current track with its album art (use the provided image assets/album_art.jpg), title "Golden Hour" by "Mara Vale" from the album "Late Summer", playback progress (1:24 of 3:52), the playback controls (play/pause, previous, next, shuffle, repeat, like), and three actions: lyrics, the queue, and song credits. Lyrics, queue, and credits each open over the player (they are actions for the current page, not views that replace the player). The track is currently playing. In-memory state only.
evals.expected_output: Art-led hero player; play/pause is the one strong fill; the three page actions sit in a floating toolbar of icon buttons (or two in the app bar); content color from the art; Google Sans Flex title

assertions.text: The lint run by `cli.mjs render` passed (it rejects raw colors, inline style or script, and misplaced type declarations)
Every render's runtimeChecks result has pass true; an incomplete check counts as a failure (unverified)
The proposal's <m3e-theme> variant is not expressive or vibrant

Lyrics, queue, and credits read as three separate, tappable controls: icon buttons in a floating toolbar, or at most two in the app bar. Not loose text buttons, and not one wide pill that looks like a single button.

evals.name: finance
evals.prompt: The home screen of a personal expense tracker called "Pocket". It must work and adapt across phone (411x923), foldable (933x704), tablet (1280x800), and desktop (1920x1080) windows; light and dark should both work. Show how much was spent this month ($1,284.50) against a monthly budget ($2,000), spending by category (Food $412, Transport $186, Home $520, Fun $166.50), the 8 most recent transactions (fake merchants, categories, dates, amounts), and a way to add a new expense. In-memory state only.
evals.expected_output: One clear hero (the total or the add action), calm neutral surfaces, category colors distinct and consistent everywhere, charts in solid roles

assertions.text: The lint run by `cli.mjs render` passed (it rejects raw colors, inline style or script, and misplaced type declarations)
Every render's runtimeChecks result has pass true; an incomplete check counts as a failure (unverified)
The proposal's <m3e-theme> variant is not expressive or vibrant

Each category keeps one visible color everywhere it appears (chart, legend, list badges), and the four categories are distinguishable by hue. Chart segments are clearly visible against their background.

evals.name: settings
evals.prompt: The Settings screen of a notes app called "Jot". It must work and adapt across phone (411x923), foldable (933x704), tablet (1280x800), and desktop (1920x1080) windows; light and dark should both work. Include: Appearance (theme: system/light/dark, use dynamic color, text size), Notifications (reminders on/off, daily summary on/off), Backup & sync (auto sync on/off, last synced "2 min ago", a "Back up now" action). The signed-in account (Sam Rivera, sam@example.com) and "About Jot" (version, privacy policy, licenses) each have their own screen elsewhere in the app; only design the Settings screen itself. In-memory state only.
evals.expected_output: Grouped segmented rows with gaps, switches for on/off, a connected button group for the theme, no version or licenses rows, one strong fill at most

assertions.text: The lint run by `cli.mjs render` passed (it rejects raw colors, inline style or script, and misplaced type declarations)
Every render's runtimeChecks result has pass true; an incomplete check counts as a failure (unverified)
The proposal's <m3e-theme> variant is not expressive or vibrant

Follows Android settings conventions: no app version, licenses, or account management rows (a link row to the account or About screen is fine); on/off settings use switches; the theme choice is a connected button group or radio choice, not a lone radio button; rows are grouped with section headings.

evals.name: trek
evals.prompt: The trip screen of a travel planner called "Wander", for an upcoming trek: "Everest Base Camp Trek", 12 days, Oct 14 to Oct 25, starting in 20 days, 4 travelers. Use the provided cover photo assets/trip_cover.jpg (a snowy Himalayan camp with yellow tents). Show today's plan preview for Day 1 (Kathmandu to Lukla flight 06:30, trek to Phakding 8 km, 3 to 4 hours, altitude 2,610 m), the day-by-day itinerary (at least 6 days with place names and altitudes: Phakding 2,610 m, Namche Bazaar 3,440 m, Namche acclimatization day, Tengboche 3,860 m, Dingboche 4,410 m, Lobuche 4,940 m), a packing checklist progress (18 of 32 items packed), and a way to open the full packing list and to share the trip. It must work and adapt across phone (411x923), foldable (933x704), tablet (1280x800), and desktop (1920x1080) windows; light and dark should both work. In-memory state only.
evals.expected_output: Photo-led layout with a visual idea tied to the trek, distinct forms for summary, plan, and itinerary, calm surfaces

assertions.text: The lint run by `cli.mjs render` passed (it rejects raw colors, inline style or script, and misplaced type declarations)
Every render's runtimeChecks result has pass true; an incomplete check counts as a failure (unverified)
The proposal's <m3e-theme> variant is not expressive or vibrant
Different information gets different forms (for example a summary, a timeline, and an itinerary are not all the same card), and text over the photo stays readable.
